artifacts.summary: 6-phase, 5-hour plan: amend the git-workflow rule's wrong premise first, then add a stash_revert guard detector, wire both escape-hatch registration points, land a red-then-green fixture, and redeploy.

memory_candidates.content: The destructive-git guard's DESTRUCTIVE_ACTION_CLASS vocabulary is registered in TWO independently hand-maintained enumerations, not one: scripts/lib/push-grant-lib.sh's PG_ACTION_CLASSES string (which gates pg_grant_mint/verify and fails CLOSED on an unregistered name) and hooks/please-grant.sh's own case "$TEXT" mint-grammar arms plus its accepted-forms error text. push-grant-lib.sh's header claims to be 'the single place that list is defined', which is true for VALIDATION but false for MINTABILITY. Registering a new class in only the first leaves the /please grant route silently unusable while the snapshot-marker route works -- an asymmetry that reads as 'the grant system doesn't support this'. By contrast, the guard hook itself needs no change: both its grant check and its snapshot-marker exemption are unconditional on the class VALUE, so a new detector only has to set the string. Pattern: when adding a destructive action class, touch both enumerations and the hook detector; three sites, not one.
